B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official launch documentation describes the MCP connector as free. A free CourtListener account is required. Higher API access is available through Free Law Project membership or commercial agreement; exact MCP-specific prices were not found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: CourtListener accounts and standard API access are free; elevated access is offered through membership or commercial agreements. Specific membership amounts were not located in the collected evidence.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Usage follows CourtListener API rate limits and account access level. Membership may increase limits. The server README says requests are subject to the API limits and refers users to the API documentation for current values; no MCP-specific per-call fee or credit price was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires CourtListener sign-in and OAuth consent, or a CourtListener API token for clients unable to use interactive OAuth. Higher limits require membership or a commercial agreement. No client allowlist, admin switch, or regional endpoint restriction was found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls authentication and API limits; the user controls account credentials and consent; membership/commercial access is arranged with Free Law Project.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted server exposes 19 tools, registered in the server implementation. They cover search and retrieval, document reading, citation extraction and verification, API access, usage checks, alerts, docket subscriptions, and document requests. The server applies input-schema validation and translates upstream errors.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results are JSON serialized into text content. Tool errors may be translated to validation, authorization, rate-limit, connection, or upstream API errors.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The inspected server code registers tools and HTTP routes; no MCP resources are registered or documented.
No MCP prompt registrations were found. The server does send global initialize instructions; those are described under Other.

The documentation describes standard request logs containing timestamps, IP addresses, and response codes, retained for operational debugging. Tool-call metrics count outcomes and credential types; deployed metrics are not publicly reachable.
No MCP sampling capability or use of sampling was found in the inspected server implementation.
No roots capability or root-dependent behavior was found in the inspected server implementation.

The supplied protected-resource metadata returns HTTP 200 and identifies the same host as authorization server. The authorization-server metadata advertises Dynamic Client Registration, authorization-code and refresh-token grants, S256 PKCE, response type `code`, token auth methods `none` and `private_key_jwt`, plus a revocation endpoint. The endpoint challenge returns HTTP 401 with `Bearer scope="api"` and a protected-resource metadata URL. Supported scopes are `openid`, `api`, `wiki`, `email`, and `profile`. The README says OAuth tokens are short-lived but gives no lifetime; it documents a separate non-expiring API-token option.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized requests return HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header. README states expired or revoked OAuth tokens trigger a 401 and clients should refresh or repeat OAuth.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration at https://mcp.courtlistener.com/register; authorization-code and refresh-token grants; S256 PKCE; token endpoint auth `none` or `private_key_jwt`; scopes_supported: `openid`, `api`, `wiki`, `email`, `profile`; revocation endpoint https://mcp.courtlistener.com/revoke; token lifetime: short-lived, exact duration NOT FOUND. API-token alternative uses `Authorization: Token <token>` and does not expire.

FastMCP server initialization supplies global instructions covering dataset scope, tool choice, semantic versus keyword search, field filtering, document retrieval, and URL construction. The code also serves an HTTP health endpoint and exposes non-public hosted metrics.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. The 19-tool code list includes read-only research and account-changing tools. Tool annotations are set in code: read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world hints are present; the generic `call_endpoint` is marked read-only even though it proxies multiple API endpoints.
2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval flow was found. Documentation says the client should ask confirmation before account-changing tools.
3. OAuth metadata scopes are `openid`, `api`, `wiki`, `email`, `profile`; tool access is based on CourtListener account credentials and API permissions. API tokens grant the account's full API access. Exact token lifetime is not published; OAuth tokens are described as short-lived. Revocation and refresh are supported.
4. No read-only mode, toolset filter, query-free mode, sandbox, or regional hosted variant was found. Local stdio and hosted HTTP modes are documented. `call_endpoint` can access the endpoints in its schema, including alert and prayer endpoints.
5. The README says no other tool inputs or outputs are persisted; exceptions are short-lived per-user pagination/citation state and a shared 24-hour document-text cache. API tokens are forwarded upstream; OAuth token storage/handling is described in the README. No field masking or PII exclusion was found.
6. API rate limits apply; search/list tools return up to 100 items per call (default 20); citation analysis verifies about 250 unique citations per call before returning a job ID; document reading chunks by default at 8,000 characters, with up to 10 chunks per call; document search supports up to 10 IDs and returns up to 20 matches per document. Pray requests have a daily per-user cap. Rate-limit errors may point to membership upgrades.
7. Code validates inputs against JSON schemas, rejects additional arguments where schemas disallow them, decodes JSON-encoded values, coerces integral floats to integers, and supports argument aliases (for example `query` to `q` in search). No operator defaults that override user-supplied values were found.
8. Documentation says request logs contain timestamps, IP addresses, and response codes for operational debugging. Tool-call outcome and credential-type metrics exist; hosted `/metrics` is not public.
9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report tool appears in the official tool list. Rate-limit errors include a membership-upgrade URL, a vendor-interest mechanism in results.
10. Global server instructions and tool descriptions shape agent behavior but are not enforcement. No skill-loading tool was found.
11. Redis-backed session state includes pagination cursors and citation jobs, keyed per user and expiring after one hour of inactivity. Document text cache is shared across users for 24 hours.
12. The hosted endpoint is a single server with a flat tool list. `call_endpoint` is a broad API proxy; citation analysis also calls CourtListener APIs.
13. `call_endpoint` is a generic API access tool, bounded by its endpoint enum and query schema. No arbitrary SQL, shell, or script execution tool was found.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: CourtListener's website and REST API also support data services and operations not exposed as dedicated MCP tools, including database replication with SQL, bulk-data downloads, webhooks, and REST endpoints not covered by the `call_endpoint` endpoint enum or its query interface. The MCP generic tool covers many API endpoints but is not documented as a complete replacement for every REST function. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: For alert, subscription, and Pray and Pay tools, the README says: “Your client should prompt you for confirmation before calling them; if it doesn't, you can manage alerts at [courtlistener.com/profile/alerts/](https://www.courtlistener.com/profile/alerts/).” This is client guidance, not server-enforced confirmation. The global initialize instructions also recommend tool sequencing and data-selection practices; see D.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The README states that only necessary account data is read or written; tool inputs and outputs are not persisted except described session state and document caching; and request logs are retained for operational debugging. The terms say agent calls using a user's credentials are treated as the user's requests and warn users to review account-changing actions. The policy also explains that data sent to the server passes through the AI provider and is subject to that provider's policy.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The documentation describes the MCP as free to use with a CourtListener account, provides access to legal research records and API tools, and says Pray and Pay requests do not charge the user but are neither immediate nor guaranteed. The terms warn that outputs are not legal advice and may be inaccurate or incomplete.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Code supports argument validation, quota/error handling, session-state expiry, document caching, and metrics. Confirmation recommendations are text-only. Privacy and retention statements are documented; implementation code supports the stated state/cache behavior, while request-log retention and deletion promises are not fully verifiable from the public server code alone.

contradictions: The official README and code expose 19 tools. Anthropic's connector listing enumerates 14 and omits `read_document`, `search_document`, `pray_for_document`, `withdraw_prayer`, and `get_api_usage`. Resolute AIM also reports 14, while the official list is 19.

The OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises `api`, `wiki`, `email`, and `profile` scopes in addition to `openid`; the README's client setup instructions say users approve `openid` and `api`. The metadata list is broader than the scopes called out in that setup step.

The server code marks `call_endpoint` read-only, while its endpoint enum includes `alerts`, `docket-alerts`, and `prayers`; the README separately identifies dedicated tools that modify account state. This makes the annotation narrower in implication than the breadth of the generic endpoint proxy.
observations_for_research: The official initialize instructions include numerous workflow preferences, including semantic-search strategy and preferred document-reading tools.
The API proxy is marked read-only in its MCP annotation but accepts endpoint selection and query parameters for multiple API surfaces.
The server's rate-limit error message can include a direct membership-upgrade link.
Document text caching is shared across users and keyed by document ID, whereas pagination and citation-job state is user-keyed and expires after inactivity.
